newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products steady to weaker in slow market.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products steady to weaker in slow market.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were steady to softer on Wednesday amid thin demand, traders said.

Gas oil shed $2.75 on a NYMEX-inspired fall in futures but premiums were stable. A 25,000-30,000 tonne cargo of heating oil changed hands at fob high quotes +$2.50 basis Italy, around unchanged. A cargo traded at high cif quotes +$0.50 basis Genoa late on Tuesday.

Traders saw plenty of heating oil availability but scant demand. Only two buyers emerged, one seeking a cargo loading in late December and another seeking a vessel loading in the first half of January.
Low sulphur diesel was long. Two Algerians are due to load at Skikda in late December and one in early January.
Naphtha prices were steady in quiet activity.
A 27,000 tonne Libyan cargo was believed sold on Tuesday at a premium to high quotes into Lavera, France for prompt delivery, traders said.
But a source said there were now no bids in the Med and the market was relatively balanced.
Gasoline was steady with most December business done and a good deal of first half January programmes already completed due to the year-end holidays.

"There is possibly one cargo that can be sold for the rest of the year...but that is the maximum," one trader said. "We see length but not much...Coming into the end of the year everyone is pretty well balanced."
Fuel oil activity in the Med was almost non-existant.

"Nothing serious is going to be done before Christmas," said one dealer. High sulphhur cracked was pegged at $107-108 fob. Bunker material was required for Gibralter and a major looked for 25kt of high sulphur straight run. M-40 was pegged close to $130 cif with hard-to-source Suez material around $125-127 cif.
